scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Lists can grow, shrink and reorder. Today we learn the methods that do it.

scenes.onScreen: "Changing a list": three numbered lines (1. insert(i, x) puts x at position i; 2. pop() takes the last item out and gives it back; 3. remove(x) deletes the first x) and an analogy card: a queue at a fish stall: someone can join at a place, the last person can leave, or you can ask a named person to leave
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: Lists come with methods that change them. Insert puts an item at a chosen position. Pop takes the last item out, and gives it back to you. Remove deletes the first item with a given value. Think of a queue at a fish stall. Someone can join at any place. The last person can leave. Or you can ask a named person to leave. All of these change the same list in place.

scenes.onScreen: queue.py: a food list that grows and shrinks
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right; faint indent guide lines
scenes.narration: [HL 1] A list of two foods. [HL 2] Insert curry at position one. Everything from position one moves along. [HL 3] The list is now fish, curry, rice. [HL 4] Pop takes the last item out, and returns it. We tie it to the name last. [HL 5] Rice. [HL 6] The list has lost its last item. [HL 7] Remove deletes the first item equal to fish. [HL 8] Only curry is left.

code.source:
food = ["fish", "rice"]
food.insert(1, "curry")
print(food)
last = food.pop()
print(last)
print(food)
food.remove("fish")
print(food)

scenes.onScreen: food tied to a list of one item; last tied to the string rice
scenes.animation: Name tags pop in with their arrows to the objects (value and type shown, no addresses); when Python reads a name the arrow glows and the object lights up
scenes.narration: Here is the picture after the code. Food is tied to a list with one item, curry. Last is tied to the string rice, which pop handed back. The string rice was removed from the list, but it still exists, because we tied a name to it. If we do not, Python removes it.

scenes.onScreen: check.py: questions you can ask a list
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 1] A list with fish twice. [HL 2] Count tells us how many times fish appears. Two. [HL 3] Index tells us the position of rice. Zero, one, two, three. So three. [HL 4] And the word in asks a yes or no question. Is curry in the list? True. Use in before remove, to be safe.

code.source:
food = ["fish", "curry", "fish", "rice"]
print(food.count("fish"))
print(food.index("rice"))
print("curry" in food)

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the command types with key-tick, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as check dot py. In the terminal, type python, space, check dot py. Two, then three, then True.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One: insert puts an item at a chosen position. Two: pop takes the last item out and returns it. Three: remove deletes the first matching item. Four: Use the word in to check before you remove. Pause the video, and say these ideas out loud, once, slowly.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: removing something that is not there
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the Python error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding

bug.error:
Python output (exactly as Python prints it):

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "queue.py", line 2, in <module>
    food.remove("prawn")
    ~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^
ValueError: list.remove(x): x not in list
bug.fixed:
food = ["fish", "rice"]
if "prawn" in food:
    food.remove("prawn")
print(food)
bug.why: remove raises a ValueError when the item is not in the list, so check with the word in first.

shorts.title: Insert and append
shorts.hook: "Append adds an item at the end of a list."
shorts.script: Append adds an item at the end of a list. Insert adds an item at any position you choose. Food dot insert, one, curry puts curry at position one, and everything after it moves along by one place. Both methods change the list in place. Use append when order does not matter, and insert when it does. Print the list to see the result. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Add at any place.

shorts.title: Pop
shorts.hook: "Pop takes an item out of a list, and gives it back to you."
shorts.script: Pop takes an item out of a list, and gives it back to you. With no number, it takes the last item. With a number, it takes the item at that position. So you can save the popped value in a name. That is useful for undo buttons, stacks, and queues. The list gets shorter, and you keep the item you took out. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Take one out.

shorts.title: Remove and in
shorts.hook: "Remove deletes the first item that equals a value."
shorts.script: Remove deletes the first item that equals a value. Food dot remove, fish, finds the first fish and deletes it. If the item is not there, Python raises an error. So check first with the word in. The question, is prawn in food, gives True or False. Use it in an if, and remove only when it is safe. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Check before you remove.

shorts.title: Value error
shorts.script: Here is the bug. You call remove on something that is not in the list. Python says, value error, x not in list. Remove does not quietly skip a missing item. It stops your program. The fix is easy. Write an if with the word in, and only remove when the item is really there. Make it a habit for every remove. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
shorts.caption: Guard your remove.

shorts.title: Pun and challenge
shorts.hook: "Why did the list get kicked out of the queue?"
shorts.script: Why did the list get kicked out of the queue? It kept popping up at the end. Your challenge. Start with the list a, b, c. Insert x at position one. Pop the last item. Then print the list. Can you predict the answer before you run it? Write your prediction in the comments, then run the code to check. Keep coding, says Xecxec! Full video: EP 26.
